main_text.p: suo beneplacito, nullamque in iis quos elegit rationem aut causam fuisse cur eli-gerentur, quæcunque tandem illa esse putetur: nullam in iis quos reprobauit causam extitisse cur reprobarentur, quæ non pariter existeret in aliis. Adeo ut cum Electio tum Reprobatio absoluta sit, nec ulla rei cuiusquam præuisione nitatur.
Amyraldus eandem doctrinam cum cæteris orthodoxis amplectitur[?], eamque & explicauit, & confirmauit rationibus inuictis ductis præsertim ex cap. 9./Epistolæ ad Rom. cap. 13. Defensionis Caluini.

Circa tertium caput, Arminianorum opinio est, Vocationem hominum confistere duntaxat in illuminatione quadam intellectus, quæ voluntatem relinquit in æquilibrio pendentem, vt Christum amplecti & non amplecti pariter queat pro arbitrio. Ita vt neminem Deus vocet ad fidem in Iesum Christum, qui non adeo resistere possit ei vocationi, vt eam reddat inutilem atque frustraneam.

page.notes: Doubtful reading: "amplectitur" on the last line is [?]; the ligature is hard to read. The end of the second paragraph lies beyond the cut. A small printed mark (an asterisk-like sign) stands in the left margin beside "opinio"; it is a printer's mark, not a note with text. "9./Epistolæ" shows a slash between the number and the title as printed; the reading of this mark is doubtful.
